**HidHide Drivers v1.2.122 – Quick Analysis & Take‑aways**

| Item | What it means |
|------|----------------|
| **Release date** | 17 h ago – very recent, so any bugs are likely still being ironed out. |
| **Commits since release** | 2 commits to `master` – minor tweaks or hot‑fixes, nothing major. |
| **Supported OS** | Windows 10/11, 64‑bit, Intel/AMD only.  No 32‑bit or older Windows support. |
| **Installation** | Standard installer → reboot.  No extra steps. |
| **Bug fixes** | 1. **Removed startup Internet connectivity check** (#102) – fixes installer failure on AtlasOS and improves offline installability. 2. **Added missing ETW manifest** (#78) – enables Windows Event Tracing for driver diagnostics/debugging. 3. **New signing certificate** – addresses a rare edge‑case where signature validation failed in WinAPI or third‑party tools. |
| **Why the ETW manifest matters** | Allows developers and advanced users to capture driver logs via ETW, making troubleshooting far easier. |
| **Why the new certificate matters** | Driver signing is mandatory for Windows 10/11.  The new cert ensures the driver passes all signature checks, preventing install errors on systems that enforce strict validation. |
| **Limitations** | • Only 64‑bit Windows 10/11.  • No mention of support for Windows Server or older OSes.  • No new features beyond bug fixes. |
| **Overall impression** | A solid, maintenance‑type update that cleans up known issues and improves reliability.  If you’re running a supported OS and need the latest stable driver, this is the version to use.  If you’re on a 32‑bit system or an older Windows version, you’ll need to look elsewhere. |

### Bottom‑line conclusions

1. **Stable & reliable** – the update removes a known startup bug and improves driver diagnostics.  
2. **Better signing** – the new certificate mitigates rare signature‑validation failures, so you’re less likely to hit install errors.  
3. **Limited scope** – no new features, just fixes; only works on 64‑bit Windows 10/11.  
4. **Recommended** – If you’re on a supported platform, upgrade to v1.2.122.  If you’re on a different OS or need additional functionality, you’ll need to wait for a future release or look for an alternative driver.
